title: Favorite drummers and left-handed drummers
summary: He admired Cottrell, Chinee Foster and Alfred Williams, and he and Russell discuss left-handed drummers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. Who were your favorite drummers when you were young? Of course I know you must have liked Cottrell or you wouldn't have taken lessons.

Yeah, I liked him and Chani and I were good friends. And I learned a whole lot from him and he was interested in me and another fellow I was interested in playing, I used to like, he was playing with Alfred Williams. Oh yes, yes.
He just died a year or two ago now. Good drummer. Yeah.
And I was interested around him so the fellas got out and learned different things, you know.
Yeah, Alfred is left handed, I guess you're right handed, are you? Yeah, right hand drummer.
Uh huh. And uh... Joe Watkins is left handed too. There are two here. Uh huh. And most left handed drummers are good drummers. Can you remember any other left handed drummers around?

Uh huh. You know, uh, yeah I know, Clay Bair, uh, he's about to play trumpet there. He played with, uh, his name is Orny. I can't think now. He played with, uh, George Lewis. Little short bright fella.
Yeah, I can't think. Because I knew another...

George Lewis, something like that. I knew another left hand drummer in Chicago, Snaggs Jones. He left here very early though. Played with King Oliver, now way back. He was left handed. Um, we were talking about some of your favorite drummers. Do you remember any others on parade that you used to like?
